question: The central stretch of the Western Coastal Plains of India is known as the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannad plains**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The central stretch is called the Kannad Plain
 
• It is primarily located in the state of Karnataka.
 
• It extends from the **Arabian Sea** in the west to the foothills of the **Western Ghats** in the east.
 
• The Kannada Plain is characterized by a mix of flat land and low-lying hills, making it less rugged compared to the adjacent Western Ghats.
 
• The soil in the Kannada Plain is primarily **alluvial** and **lateritic**, conducive to farming

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6db57fadbe13a39345f50aaa968c0b5bd4c67f3c78c787a2625a2bcf7a4159b9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Peninsular plateau is flanked by stretch of narrow coastal strips, running along the Arabian Sea on the west and the Bay of Bengal on the east.
 
• The Western Coastal Plains
 
 
• The western coast, sandwiched between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, is a narrow plain.
 
• It consists of three sections; the northern part of the coast is called the Konkan__ (Mumbai – Goa),
 
 
• while the southern stretch is referred to as the Malabar Coast.
 
 
 
• The rivers flowing through this coastal plain do not form any delta.
 
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains 
 
 
• The eastern coast are the plains along the Bay of Bengal are wide and level.
 
• In the northern part, it is referred to as the Northern Circar, while the southern part is known as the Coromandel Coast.
 
• There are well-developed deltas here, formed by the rivers flowing eastward in to the Bay of Bengal and include the deltas of the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri.
